corrections.claimed_speedup: Level 9: aocl-zlib 27.47 MB/s compress, 439.38 MB/s decompress, ratio 32.21% versus zlib 1.3.2 7.37 MB/s, 212.55 MB/s, 31.91% (about 3.7x and 2.1x, derived from page data). PR summary: zlib up to 3.7x compression and 2x decompression, bzip2 2.1-2.3x compress and +60-69% decompress, snappy +20% compress and 2x decompress, zstd +14-21% compress and +8-10% decompress. lz4 1.10.0 381.25 / 2499.41 MB/s versus aocl-lz4 400.32 / 2550.71 MB/s, about +5% and +2% (derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from an open (unmerged) lzbench pull request written by an AMD developer, not a neutral run; inikep requested changes on 2026-09-19 citing seven concerns including buffer allocation impacts, symbol linking and outdated vendored code (5.3.0 versus 5.3.2). The repo README itself carries no numbers. The compress speedup is for level 9 where stock zlib is slow, and aocl-zlib ratio is slightly worse (32.21% versus 31.91%); aocl-zstd also loses some ratio (31.94% versus 31.20% at -3). Not compared against zlib-ng or libdeflate on that page. Gains are small on lz4 (+5% / +2%) and moderate on zstd. Tuned for AMD Zen CPUs. Mixed per-file licenses (BSD-3-Clause, MIT, NCSA, all OSI) plus upstream zlib, zstd, bzip2 licenses.
